blockers.target: NIK.efq / NIK.orE cross-label soundness under the generalized induction motive
blockers.verbatim_goal: CKForces r v botForces (ρ y) A -- from ih: CKForces r v botForces (ρ x) Proposition.bot (i.e. botForces (ρ x)), for arbitrary A and an adversarially-chosen ρ with y ∉ G.X ∪ ctxLabels Γ (unconstrained by raw edge-cond and Γ-cond, since NIK.efq places no relation between x and y)
blockers.root_cause: NIK.efq/NIK.orE are cross-label with the conclusion label fully independent of the premise label (unlike boxE/diaI, which always carry a TClosure edge, or boxI/diaE, whose fresh label is added to G.X via addEdge before use). A machine-verified two-point countermodel (lean_run_code, this dispatch) shows botForces need not propagate to an r/≤-disconnected point even under every cs5FCIncest + CKValidFC hypothesis, so the naive universally-quantified-ρ motive is false for this case, independent of the specific proof term.
blockers.what_was_tried: Direct transcription attempt of the generalized motive per the plan; verification that boxI/diaE/boxE/diaI close cleanly under it; construction and lean_run_code verification of a countermodel refuting the efq case specifically; assessment of two candidate fixes (a not-yet-landed 'IsDerivationForest built from Graph.trivial via addEdge chain implies G.X is TClosure-TS5-total' connectivity lemma, and an existential-motive reformulation) -- both assessed as out-of-phase-8-scope, re-plan-sized work.
blockers.what_is_needed: A dedicated follow-up phase/task to (1) prove the connectivity lemma and (2) reformulate the main induction's motive existentially, re-verifying all 12 constructors against the new motive. See handoffs/08_phase8-blocked-crosslabel-efq.md for the full analysis and recommended scope.
